correctness.rationale: All-k proof reduces unordered representations to B+B,3B+3B and B+3B. The exact digit-product formula incorporates positive-summand subtraction and diagonals, and the two-carry-state base-nine intersection count gives 2^(2k-1). Inclusion–exclusion and pure-support exceptional-class classifications algebraically yield 8*5^(k-1)-2^(2k-1)-5k. Exhaustive brute-force counts match every n<9^k for k<=4, with additional 5,6 formula-count checks; finite computations corroborate rather than prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The exact number of nonuniquely representable integers is a natural missing invariant in a canonical, balanced periodic digit-partition minimal basis. It sharpens the established density-one uniqueness theorem to a complete all-k census and the sharp exponent log_9 5. The powers 9^k are intrinsic full two-position digit blocks, not an arbitrary numerical slice; the count requires an exact carry-state intersection and nontrivial pure-support boundary corrections.
